rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say the verse proves only that Jesus could perform the signs if asked, not that any occurred; al-Tabataba'i rejects this limitation.
rows.anchor: فساد ما ذكره بعضهم أن قصارى ما تدل عليه الآية أن الله سبحانه جعل في عيسى ابن مريم هذا السر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus's report of what people ate and stored was a further, explicit and verifiable disclosure of unseen knowledge, which belongs to God and those messengers He informs.
rows.anchor: وهذا إخبار بالغيب المختص بالله تعالى ومن خصه من رسله بالوحي وهو آية أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The permission formula is omitted for this announcement because it is speech performed by Jesus, whereas creating and reviving are truly God's acts attributed to others only by His permission.
rows.anchor: عبر عنها بالإنباء وهو كلام قائم بعيسى عليه السلام يعد فعلا له فلا يليق أن يسند إلى ساحة القدس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creating birds and reviving the dead could mislead simple listeners into deifying Jesus, while people may treat hidden knowledge as attainable by ascetics or soothsayers; hence those signs require the permission qualifier.
rows.anchor: فإن القلوب الساذجة تقبل ألوهية خالق الطير ومحيي الموتى بأدنى وسوسة ومغلطة

words: إن في ذلك لآية لكم إن كنتم مؤمنين
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For healing, simply identifying it as God's sign suffices; Jesus addresses people who claim belief and challenges them to be sincere in that claim.
rows.anchor: أي إن كنتم صادقين في دعواكم الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Confirming what is before me” coordinates with “a messenger to the Children of Israel”; the shift from third to first person is sound because the latter phrase is construed as Jesus saying, “I have come to you.”
rows.anchor: وكون المعطوف مبنيا على التكلم مع كون المعطوف عليه مبنيا على الغيبة أعني كون عيسى عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus confirms the original Torah revealed to Moses, as God taught it to him; confirming the Torah present in his time does not prove that text uncorrupted, just as Muhammad's confirmation does not.
rows.anchor: وهي التوراة الأصل النازلة على موسى عليهما السلام فلا دلالة لكونه مصدقا للتوراة التي في زمانه

words: ولأحل لكم بعض الذي حرم عليكم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God had forbidden Jews some good things for their wrongdoing; Jesus's mission therefore upheld Torah rulings except for certain burdensome laws God abrogated through him.
rows.anchor: فإن الله تعالى قد حرم عليهم بعض الطيبات قال تعالى فبظلم من الذين هادوا حرمنا عليهم طيبات

words: ولأحل لكم بعض الذي حرم عليكم
rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A reported view is that the Gospel contains no independent legal code, consistent with Jesus affirming Torah except for laws abrogated through him.
rows.anchor: ولذا قيل إن الإنجيل غير مشتمل على الشريعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose lām in “so I may make lawful” coordinates with “with a sign from your Lord”; Jesus came in order to abrogate some prohibitions imposed on them.
rows.anchor: واللام للغاية والمعنى قد جئتكم لأنسخ بعض الأحكام المحرمة المكتوبة عليكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated sign statement clarifies that “fear God and obey me” follows from the sign, not merely from making some forbidden things lawful.
rows.anchor: فهو لدفع الوهم ويمكن أن يكون هو مراد من قال

rows.speaker: من قال
rows.claim: One explanation of the repeated statement is that it separates the material before it from what follows; al-Tabataba'i says mere separation is no rhetorical merit.
rows.anchor: فهو لدفع الوهم ويمكن أن يكون هو مراد من قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus declares God his and their Lord to remove any excuse for deifying him, whether he discerned that belief among them or learned it by revelation; 5:117 indicates God commanded this clarification.
rows.anchor: فيه قطع لعذر من اعتقد ألوهيته لتفرسه عليه السلام ذلك منهم أو لعلمه بذلك بالوحي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The annunciation story briefly covers Jesus from conception to mission, then resumes with his disciples, his people's plot, God's counterplot, his purification, taking, and raising to complete his story.
rows.anchor: اقتصر عليها اقتصاصا إيجازا في الكلام وفرع عليها تتمة الجملة من قصته وهو انتخابه حوارييه ومكر قومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account selects what mattered for the Christians of Najran, who came to Medina to debate; other details of Jesus's story in several surahs are omitted.
rows.anchor: وهم نصارى نجران الوفد الذين أتوا المدينة للبحث والاحتجاج ولذلك أسقط منها بعض الخصوصيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using “perceived” for inward disbelief suggests it became outwardly evident, or that Jesus sensed their intent to harm and kill him because of it.
rows.anchor: في استعمال لفظ الإحساس في مورد الكفر مع كونه أمرا قلبيا إشعارا بظهوره منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus seeks a core group to distinguish itself for truth, stabilize and concentrate the religious mission's strength, and let the call spread; powers need such a center or dissipate.
rows.anchor: أن يتميز عدة من رجال قومه فيتمحضوا للحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pledges of al-Aqaba and beneath the tree likewise gathered and anchored the Prophet's community's strength so the Islamic call could endure.
rows.anchor: ونظير ذلك في دعوة الإسلام بيعة العقبة وبيعة الشجرة أراد بها رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeing that most or all Israelites would reject him and might silence him, ending the mission, Jesus prepared a group of believers as its foundation, spreading faith and proof against disbelief.
rows.anchor: فلما أيقن عيسى عليه السلام أن دعوته غير ناجحة في بني إسرائيل كلهم أو جلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adding “to God” heightens the appeal and encouragement in the question, as in the image of lending God a good loan.
rows.anchor: الذي سيق لأجله هذا الاستفهام نظير قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition attaches to “my helpers” by construing help as traveling or proceeding toward God; Abraham's “I am going to my Lord” offers a parallel.
rows.anchor: بتضمين النصرة معنى السلوك والذهاب أو ما يشابههما

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some interpreters take إلى to mean “with”; al-Tabataba'i rejects this for lack of evidence and because it would put God alongside other helpers and contradict Jesus's and the disciples' manner of speech.
rows.anchor: وأما ما احتمله بعض المفسرين من كون إلى بمعنى مع فلا دليل عليه ولا يساعد أدب القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A ḥawārī is a person's specially close companion; it is also said to derive from ḥawr, intense whiteness, and the Qur'an uses it only for Jesus's special companions.
rows.anchor: حواري الإنسان من اختص به من الناس وقيل أصله من الحور وهو شدة البياض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disciples explain being God's helpers by saying they believe in God; this supports reading “to God” as a path, since faith is the path to Him.
rows.anchor: فإنه يفيد معنى السلوك في الطريق إلى الله والإيمان طريق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One may infer from 61:14 that the disciples' response was faith after earlier faith; al-Tabataba'i sees no difficulty because faith and submission have different ranks.
rows.anchor: ربما استفيد من قوله تعالى كما قال عيسى ابن مريم للحواريين من أنصاري إلى الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author also cites God's command to the disciples in 5:111 as a possible indication that their answer to Jesus was faith after earlier faith.
rows.anchor: بل ربما دل قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their appeal to God as submitters, together with their fuller prayer, describes complete surrender possible only for purified believers, not people who merely testify to monotheism and prophethood.
rows.anchor: وهذا الإسلام هو التسليم المطلق لجميع ما يريده الله تعالى منهم وفيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every degree of faith is preceded by a degree of Islam: initial outward submission and general testimony, then inward assent to that testimony.
rows.anchor: أن كل مرتبة من الإيمان تسبقها مرتبة من مراتب الإسلام كما يدل عليه قولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next degree of Islam is inward acceptance of faith that ends resentment toward God's and the Messenger's commands and issues in practical following; the next degree of faith is sincere action and settled servitude.
rows.anchor: التسليم القلبي لمعنى الإيمان وينقطع عنده السخط والاعتراض الباطني بالنسبة إلى جميع ما يأمر به الله ورسوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The third degree of Islam is surrender to God's love and will, with no independent desire; the third degree of faith spreads this servile surrender through all deeds.
rows.anchor: التسليم لمحبة الله وإرادته تعالى فلا يحب ولا يريد شيئا إلا بالله ولا يقع هناك إلا ما أحبه الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus first commands reverent faith in God and obedience by following His messenger, then explains their basis in their shared Lord; worship means this faith and following, the straight path leading to God.
rows.anchor: فيجب عليكم أن تتقوه بالإيمان وأن تطيعوني بالاتباع وبالجملة يجب عليكم أن تعبدوه بالتقوى وطاعة الرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus's worship and obedience form a straight path that leads the person walking it to God.
rows.anchor: فجعله سبيلا ينتهي بسالكه إلى الله سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited verse indicates that God inspired the disciples to believe in Jesus and His messenger and that they were prophets; their answer was therefore faith after faith.
rows.anchor: أن إجابتهم إنما كانت بوحي من الله تعالى إليهم وأنهم كانوا أنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus sought helpers for the straight path of worship—reverence and obedience—and the disciples answered as requested, calling themselves God's helpers and explaining this as belief and submission.
rows.anchor: ثم ذكروا ما هو كالتفسير له فقالوا

words: ربنا آمنا بما أنزلت واتبعنا الرسول
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In prayer they restate submission as following the Messenger and widen belief to all revelation Jesus taught, including scripture, wisdom, Torah, and Gospel; this is among the highest degrees of faith.
rows.anchor: فبدلوا الإسلام من الاتباع ووسعوا في الإيمان بتقييده بجميع ما أنزل الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their faith and following are not a first degree of belief but among its highest ranks.
rows.anchor: وهذا كما ترى ليس أول درجة من الإيمان بل من أعلى درجاته وأسماها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They invoke Jesus as witness to their submission and following so their account of their state before God is supported by the testimony of His Messenger.
rows.anchor: وإنما استشهدوا عيسى عليه السلام في إسلامهم واتباعهم ولم يقولوا آمنا بالله وإنا مسلمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disciples' prayer is presented as their direct words with the speech verb omitted, a subtle Qur'anic style that narrates the event itself.
rows.anchor: مقول قول الحواريين حذف القول من اللفظ للدلالة على حكاية نفس الواقعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask to be counted among witnesses because conveying revelation requires teaching it in word and deed; witnessing that transmission requires learning from the Messenger and following his practice.
rows.anchor: فالشهادة على التبليغ إنما يكون بتعلمها من الرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The witnesses are likely those who testify to delivery, as indicated by the question in 7:6 addressed to those sent and to the messengers.
rows.anchor: وهي الشهادة على التبليغ وأما قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In 5:83, “write us among the witnesses” instead testifies to the truth of the Messenger's message, not to its delivery.
rows.anchor: فهو شهادة على حقية رسالة الرسول دون التبليغ والله أعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possible reading is that, after invoking Jesus as witness, they ask to be recorded among witnesses over people's deeds, like Abraham and Ishmael's prayer.
rows.anchor: أن المسؤول أن يكتبهم الله من شهداء الأعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plotters are the Children of Israel, as the preceding statement says Jesus perceived disbelief among them; the meaning of God's counterplot was discussed at 2:26.
rows.anchor: الماكرون هم بنو إسرائيل بقرينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tawaffī means taking something fully; it is used of death because God takes a person's soul from the body at death.
rows.anchor: التوفي أخذ الشيء أخذا تاما ولذا يستعمل في الموت لأن الله يأخذ عند الموت نفس الإنسان من بدنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Considering 32:11 and 39:42, the Qur'an uses tawaffī for taking and preserving the soul, not simply dying; it assures that the soul is kept until resurrection, unlike explicit uses of “die.”
rows.anchor: إن التوفي لم يستعمل في القرآن بمعنى الموت بل بعناية الأخذ والحفظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because 4:157–159 denies that Jesus was killed or crucified, tawaffī is not explicit proof of his death; 4:159 appears to say he remains alive with God until the People of the Book believe in him, so it may mean taking him away from the Jews.
rows.anchor: فمن هذه الجهة لا صراحة للتوفي في الموت

rows.speaker: اليهود
rows.claim: Jews claimed they killed Jesus; the Qur'an cites this claim in order to deny it.
rows.anchor: فإن اليهود كانت تدعي أنهم قتلوا المسيح عيسى ابن مريم عليه السلام

rows.speaker: النصارى
rows.claim: Christians likewise believed Jesus was killed by crucifixion, though they held that God raised him from his grave afterward, as in the Gospels.
rows.anchor: وكذلك كانت تظن النصارى أن اليهود قتلت عيسى ابن مريم عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God is not in physical space, “raising you to Me” denotes spiritual elevation and nearness, like “then to Me is your return,” especially if tawaffī means taking custody.
rows.anchor: إذ لا مكان له تعالى من سنخ الأمكنة الجسمانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sense of elevation in nearness to God resembles the martyrs, who are alive with their Lord, and Enoch, whom God raised to a high station.
rows.anchor: نظير ما ذكره تعالى في حق المقتولين في سبيله

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that Jesus was raised alive, body and soul, to the physical heaven, taken as a place of nearness to God, blessing, and angels; the author defers discussion of heaven's meaning.
rows.anchor: وربما يقال إن المراد برفعه إليه رفعه بروحه وجسده حيا إلى السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because purification follows raising to God, it means spiritual separation from disbelievers and protection from living among their polluted society, not outward cleansing.
rows.anchor: أفاد معنى التطهير المعنوي دون الظاهري الصوري فهو إبعاده من الكفار وصونه عن مخالطتهم

words: وجاعل الذين اتبعوك فوق الذين كفروا
rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Commentators read this as a promise that true followers of Jesus—right-believing Christians before Islam and Muslims afterward—will surpass Jews who reject his prophethood in argument until Judgment.
rows.anchor: هذا ما ذكره وارتضاه المفسرون في معنى الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i rejects the commentators' reading: the future wording promises a later event, yet Jesus's own proofs already matched his followers' and were clearest before his raising.
rows.anchor: ومن المعلوم أن ليست حجة متبعي عيسى عليه السلام إلا حجة عيسى نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Limiting superiority of evidence to Judgment Day makes no sense if it means proof's force, which is timeless and remains true at the Resurrection according to the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: مع أن الحجة في غلبتها لا تقبل التقييد بوقت ولا يوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If superiority means greater public acceptance and strength, it implies political dominance contrary to history; a predicted end-time rise also lacks support in the wording.
rows.anchor: مرجع ذلك إما إلى تفوق متبعيه الحقيقيين من حيث السلطنة والقوة والواقع خلافه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Interpreting superiority as numerical majority also conflicts with history, since falsehood has continually outnumbered truth from Jesus's time through the author's present, and numbers do not fit the context of wrath on Jews.
rows.anchor: فلم يزل أهل الباطل يربو ويزيد جمعهم على أهل الحق من زمن عيسى إلى يومنا هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse identifies the two groups with active verbs (“those who followed” and “those who disbelieved”), describing realized acts rather than fixed attributes such as “followers” and “disbelievers.”
rows.anchor: والفعل إنما يدل على التحقق والحدوث دون التلبس الذي يدل عليه الوصف كالمتبعين والكافرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A deed by some in a community can be attributed to later members when they approve it or continue their predecessors' way, as the Qur'an holds Jews responsible for ancestors' crimes and defiance.
rows.anchor: ومجرد صدور فعل من بعض أفراد أمة مع رضاء الباقين به وسلوك اللاحقين مسلك السابقين وجريهم على طريقتهم كاف في نسبة ذلك الفعل إليهم
